channel.title: Hlido — AI agent reviews
channel.description: Independent C2PA-verified reviews of AI agents. Every claim tested, scored on the Laddoo scale, signed with cryptographic provenance.

item.title: execkit — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: A well-designed, safety-first shell-session layer built specifically for AI agents — the docs and API shape are excellent; adoption and battle-testing are what's left to prove.

item.title: RootPilot — Laddoo 71/100
item.description: A sharply-positioned automated root-cause tool for ops engineers — paste a log, get the why, not just the what — with a clean product surface and one caveat around its unshown MCP/agent story.

item.title: emailmd — Laddoo 72/100
item.description: A neat, genuinely agent-native way to write responsive emails as Markdown — an MCP server lets any AI assistant draft, lint and render them, which is the clever part.

item.title: mcp-v8 — Laddoo 80/100
item.description: A code-execution MCP server that hands an agent one run_js tool inside a locked-down V8 isolate — an ambitious 'agents write code, not tool-calls' bet with a serious security story.

item.title: SysKnife — Laddoo 81/100
item.description: A Linux sysadmin co-pilot built around the right safety primitive: the AI proposes typed actions, never shell strings, and a privileged daemon executes only what you approve.

item.title: Serena — Laddoo 84/100
item.description: An agent-first, IDE-grade semantic toolkit that plugs into any MCP client — one of the cleaner examples of tooling designed for the model, not the human.

item.title: Rover — Laddoo 66/100
item.description: A polished pitch for an AI 'customer engineer' that joins live customer calls and acts across your stack — but the surface is all promise, demo-gated, and the extraordinary claims are exactly the ones we cannot verify.

item.title: CodeGraphContext — Laddoo 76/100
item.description: A CLI-plus-MCP tool that turns a local codebase into a navigable knowledge graph for AI assistants — real adoption behind it, with marketing that oversells a bit past the evidence.

item.title: SquadCue — Laddoo 73/100
item.description: A local cockpit that turns your Claude Code sessions into named 'employees' you supervise through an approval inbox — early and single-user, but unusually honest about exactly what it is and isn't.

item.title: Twill — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: A 'software factory' that turns GitHub, Slack and Linear tasks into tested pull requests inside a warm, full-stack dev environment — a strong, concrete pitch that the public surface can't yet prove.

item.title: Cicada — Laddoo 76/100
item.description: AST-powered code intelligence for Elixir (and beta Python) delivered over MCP, with a refreshingly transparent — if vendor-run — benchmark instead of vibes.

item.title: infrabroker — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: An infrastructure access broker built on a genuinely strong idea — the model never holds a credential; it requests an action and the broker mints a single-use key for it.

item.title: srunx — Laddoo 72/100
item.description: A clean, genuinely agent-native toolkit for orchestrating SLURM jobs as code — well-executed and MCP-first, with adoption still the open question.

item.title: Vizard — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: Mature, genuinely usable AI video-clipping tool that does the one job well — held back only by a crowded field where its differentiation is thin.

item.title: WhoDunnitAI — Laddoo 60/100
item.description: A charming, genuinely working voice-driven murder-mystery game — but it's a consumer novelty, not an agent, and its durability rests on a single creator's OpenAI bill.

item.title: Trinity Lite — Laddoo 73/100
item.description: An evidence-first AgentOps control plane for cross-vendor CLI agents — thoughtfully designed around the right idea (route → review → verify → accept), with adoption the main unknown.

item.title: backscroll — Laddoo 70/100
item.description: A focused, well-documented terminal-output recorder that agents can query over MCP — does one thing precisely, with pre-1.0 maturity the only real caveat.

item.title: OneCLI — Laddoo 76/100
item.description: A network-layer firewall that treats coding-agent policy as something enforced outside the model, not requested politely inside it — and that architectural choice is the whole pitch.

item.title: Orite — Laddoo 52/100
item.description: A sharp thesis about agent trust and spending — 'the future isn't agents that can pay, it's agents you trust to pay' — wrapped around a product that, on the public surface, is still a waitlist.

item.title: Phinq — Laddoo 72/100
item.description: An MIT-licensed, install-in-two-minutes approval layer that makes an agent ask before it does anything irreversible — and proves a human was in the loop with a tamper-evident log.

item.title: hotcell — Laddoo 80/100
item.description: The most technically honest agent-sandboxing surface we have reviewed this cycle — Apache-2.0, self-hosted on hardware you already own, with a containment model spelled out down to which guarantees are kernel-enforced and which are only advisory.

item.title: agy-bridge — Laddoo 66/100
item.description: A small, unusually well-engineered MCP bridge that lets Claude Code offload token-heavy grunt work to Google's Antigravity CLI — high craft, honest about its own failure modes, but a niche tool for a specific two-CLI setup.

item.title: YepCode MCP Server — Laddoo 73/100
item.description: A clean bridge that turns any YepCode process into an MCP tool by adding a tag — genuinely low-friction for teams already on YepCode, and honestly a lock-in decision for everyone else.

item.title: Agent Manager — Laddoo 73/100
item.description: A fast, keyboard-driven control tower for running many coding agents at once — spawn in a sentence, answer a blocked one without attaching, review its diff in place — and it runs your real installed CLIs as-is rather than reimplementing them.

item.title: persistproc — Laddoo 64/100
item.description: A deliberately tiny MCP server that gives any agent shared visibility and control over your long-running dev processes — the copy-paste killer for AI coding — and its restraint (three tools, no config file) is the design, not a gap.

item.title: Axe — Laddoo 70/100
item.description: A Unix-philosophy answer to the everything-chatbot: small, single-purpose LLM agents defined in TOML and composed with cron, pipes and git hooks — a coherent design that is also refreshingly security-conscious.

item.title: Kubit — Laddoo 74/100
item.description: A mature warehouse-native product-analytics company extending into agent observability — its real edge is joining agent traces to user behaviour in your own warehouse, not another dashboard that stops at the LLM.

item.title: Agent Blueprint — Laddoo 64/100
item.description: A cleanly-designed CLI + MCP server that delivers implementation 'blueprints' to coding agents as Agent Skills directories — but the whole thing is gated behind a commercial engagement, so almost nothing about it is independently verifiable.

item.title: tailtest — Laddoo 77/100
item.description: An open-source, hook-based test generator that fires automatically on every AI code edit across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Cline — a genuinely useful answer to 'the AI wrote the code AND the tests, so who actually checked it works?'
